newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end firmer as yen falls.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end firmer as yen falls.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based gold futures reversed early losses to end firmer across the board on Monday, as the dollar was boosted against the yen on comments by a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two to six yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark October was four yen up at 1,341 yen.
Bullion was quoted at 375.75/376.05 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $376.10/60 in New York on Friday.
The dollar rose above 112 yen in late Tokyo after a BOJ official said more failures of Japanese financial institutions could not be ruled out.

In the gold futures market, private investors continued to hunt for bargains for most of the day on views that the yen will fall further in the longer term, while trade houses bought spot gold in arbitrage trade.
The bullion market was under selling pressure from overseas investors during Asian hours, absorbing sporadic buying by Japanese trade houses.
Traders said that amid the continuing bearish sentiment, spot gold could probe the downside at $375 per ounce soon.
Silver and platinum futures also ended firmer in tandem with gold.
In the platinum futures market, private investors, who were generally buying on dips earlier in the day, switched to profit-taking later.
Spot platinum was quoted at $382.25/383.00 at the Tokyo close, after opening at 382.75/383.50.
The benchmark October silver contract was up 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 178.4 yen, while benchmark October platinum futures were seven yen higher at 1,373 yen.
Palladium futures were narrowly mixed in sluggish trade. Benchmark October was three yen up at 427 yen.
